analysis.title: FX Daily Snapshot: Risk sentiment continuing to drive FX market performance
key_insights: Global equity correction deepened, led by AI-related investments. The Nasdaq composite fell -5.3% on Friday, putting it -18.4% below last month's record high and near bear market territory.

The S&P 500 closed -3.7% on Friday and is -11.9% below last month's high. Weakness is spreading from tech to broader equities. Kospi fell as much as -5.8% intraday on Monday before trimming to around -3.3%.

Safe haven demand and tighter financial conditions lifted bonds. The 10-year UST yield fell back below 5.00% to a Friday low of 4.90%. Short-end yields fell 11bps on Friday as hike expectations were pared.
Markets still price back-to-back Fed hikes in December and January. Further equity weakness into year-end would more seriously challenge that pricing.
Treasury Secretary Bessent warned the Fed risks a policy mistake by overtightening and pointed to fragility in the financial system.
FX performance last week was driven by risk-off. JPY and CHF outperformed, while high-beta AUD, SEK and NOK underperformed. MUFG expects G10 FX to stay tightly linked to risk sentiment this week.

The dollar index hit a fresh year-to-date high just below 104.00 last week but lost upward momentum late in the week. MUFG recommended a new short USD/CHF trade in its latest FX Weekly, on the risk of a USD correction if Fed hike expectations are pared further.

Commodity currencies are under pressure from falling commodity prices. The Bloomberg Commodity Price Index is down about 14% from its mid-September peak and broke its 200-day moving average for the first time since summer last year.

The index peaked just above 140, similar to the 2020-22 peak, after which prices lost about a third of their value over two years. This suggests room for further commodity FX downside, especially in AUD, COP, NOK and ZAR, which have been among the best performers since last summer.

Precious metals led the commodity reversal. Gold and silver rose about 70% and 230% between August 2025 and January 2026 and have now almost fully reversed to roughly USD3,500/oz and USD40/oz. USD/ZAR rose to just above 17.500, the highest since August 2025, mirroring gold.

The USD debasement trade has unwound. Warsh has been more hawkish than expected as Fed Chair and the Democrats won the midterms, which eased Fed independence concerns and reduced the US policy risk premium in the USD.
